curriculum.lesson_evidence: A group dance joins individual ideas into one piece. Groups choose a theme, share ideas fairly and use formations such as lines, circles and scattered shapes. Dancers can move in unison (together), in canon (one after another) or mirror each other. To compose, try ideas, keep what works and rehearse. Everyone's ideas count, and each dancer has a role.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A group disagrees about which movements to use. Write two fair ways to decide and one way to include everyone's ideas.

FEEDBACK
Ways: take turns to choose a section, or vote and use the idea with the most votes first, then use another idea in the next section. Include everyone by giving each dancer one movement to teach the group.

WATCH FOR
Believing the group dance belongs to the most confident dancer. Group dances work when everyone's ideas and abilities are used.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Compose a 30-second group dance for 3 or more people with a theme, a formation, a unison section, a canon section and a mirror section. Write the plan, rehearse and record how decisions were shared. Give a seated or smaller-movement option for each section.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

WORKED MODEL

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
